newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms to begin selling DVD players this year.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms to begin selling DVD players this year.

text.p: Toshiba Corp, Hitachi Ltd, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd and Pioneer Electronic Corp will start selling digital video disc players (DVD) later this year, companies and industry sources said on Wednesday.
DVD is a new recording system which has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs obsolete.
Sony Corp said it was planning to start selling DVD players and software next spring.

A Toshiba spokeswoman said that the company was planning to start selling DVD players in Japan and the United States simultaneously in October or in November. The price of the player will be less than 100,000 yen in Japan and between $600 and $800 in the United States, she said.
Hitachi said it was planning to start selling its DVD players in Japan in late October and abroad in December. It did not provide details of its players.
Pioneer said that it would begin sales of its DVD players in late October but it did not elaborate.
A Sony spokesman said it would begin selling DVD players in the United States, Japan and the other parts of Asia in the spring of next year. Sales in Europe would begin in mid 1997, he said.
Details of Matsushita's DVD players were not immediately available but the company is expected to hold a news conference on DVD on Thursday.
